topology_reasoning.what_the_device_is: A loop-embedded dual-arm interferometer: a closed stadium-shaped loop waveguide (rounded-rectangle ring) whose left and right inner walls, at mid-height, each launch a wide hub stub that fans out through a Y-junction into two branches. The branches feed two parallel horizontal arm waveguides (top and bottom) that bridge the left and right Y-junctions. Each arm carries, on its outer side, a slotted loading structure: an outer rail parallel to the arm, tied to the arm by three posts, forming two closed rectangular windows per arm. The whole figure is mirror-symmetric left-right and (to ~1 px) top-bottom.
topology_reasoning.how_it_works: Read as a Sagnac/loop-mirror-embedded Mach-Zehnder: the loop carries light to the left hub, the Y-junction splits it into the two arms, and the right Y-junction recombines it back into the loop; interference between the two arm paths sets the transfer function. The two-window slotted rails on each arm's outer side read as loading segments (phase-shifter electrodes or Bragg-like perturbation segments) that set the differential phase/coupling of the arms. Function is therefore governed by the arm path-length balance, the arm separation, the guide width, and the loading-segment geometry.
topology_reasoning.anisotropy_note: footprint.json + the deterministic calibration map the image x-axis to 3.0 um and y-axis to 5.5 um (517.0 vs 141.82 px/um). The landscape image is therefore a ~3.65x horizontally-stretched rendering of a portrait 3.0 x 5.5 um device: circular-looking arcs in the image are ellipses in um space (outer corner ellipse ~0.946 x 2.489 um), and the visually-thick ring sides are only ~0.31 um wide while top/bottom walls are ~0.52-0.54 um. All geometry below is specified in um space against this calibration.
function_defining_knobs: delta_length (um): path-length imbalance between top and bottom arm - THE interferometer knob; 0.0 as drawn (symmetric arms). Perturbing it physically lengthens the top arm waveguide.
arm_pitch (um): center-to-center separation of the two arm guides (1.033 as drawn); with wg_width sets the arm gap.
arm_length (um): length of each arm's straight interaction section (0.892 as drawn).
wg_width (um): arm guide width (0.247 top / 0.240 bottom as drawn).
slot_len / slot_h / rail_t / post_w / mid_post_w (um): loading-structure geometry (window size, outer-rail thickness, post widths).
ring walls + corner radii: loop geometry (ring_wall_side ~0.311, ring_wall_top ~0.522, ring_wall_bot ~0.536, corner ellipse 0.946x2.489 outer / 0.708x1.735 inner).
topology_reasoning.construction_plan: Catalog primitives only: rounded-rect ring = boolean NOT of two stadium shapes, each the union of two rectangles + four corner ellipses (gf.components.rectangle, gf.components.ellipse); hubs, branches, arms, rails, posts = rectangles; Y-junction diagonals = 2-point gf.Path extruded at constant um width (slope 2.188, width 0.214); the four windows = rectangle subtraction from the solid rail+post box. Core mirrored about x=1.4981 (measured device center), ring about x=1.5. Script writes lengths.json (arm centerline lengths from gf.Path objects) so homi.spec_optimization.verify_knob_response can prove delta_length moves real geometry (area growth ~= wg_width * delta).

iterations.change_made: Initial parametric build from pixel measurements: elliptical-corner stadium ring (outer minus inner), hub slabs, extruded Y-junction diagonals, branch bands, arm bars, slotted loading boxes with window cuts.

Per-corner area-weighted ellipse fits (8 corners); half-pixel raster-bleed bias on all white-facing bottom/right edges (PIL inks the boundary line, and 1 nm dbu snap made borderline rows flip); exact per-window cut rects; elbow + hub-tip fillet patches; measured diagonal mirror axis 2.7465.

Fixed double-applied bias on branch bands (bias was already in the constants); top-right window top edge corrected to row 237 (bbox min-row 235 is only a 2-col sliver); bottom window bottom edges to rows 574 (BL) / 573 (BR).

16 cut + 4 add micro-patch rects from a greedy net-gain search on the diff: staircase corrections where the target boundary is superelliptical vs my ellipses (flat-corner transitions, inner-wall flats).
Hub-tip patch trims + bottom-left window ragged-bottom split (rows 574/573 halves). Gain mostly cancelled by a 1 nm boolean sliver at the split seam (dbu position+size rounding desync).
Snap all rect coordinates to the 1 nm dbu grid before sizing so abutting rects share edges exactly; seam sliver eliminated. Final.

final.note: delta_length_um in lengths.json is 0.028 at delta_length=0.0: the honest drawn asymmetry (arm bars sit ~0.7 px below the branch axis; diagonals mirror about y=2.7465, not 2.75). The knob check verifies the response, which is exact.
